messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Julie Park <julie@montclairbio.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: UK IDTA evidence mapping + proposed SLA exception

Hi all —

Julie, thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, Montclair needs a concise map tying the UK IDTA / UK Addendum obligations to the underlying technical evidence we can provide (logs, retention policies, subprocessors, encryption attestations). To keep this slim for procurement, I attached a one-tab template (uk-idta-evidence-template.xlsx) that maps clause -> required evidence -> who owns the action.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you confirm which environments (prod/staging) will be in scope for the pilot?
- Procurement surfaced a possible SLA exception request around routing: they want formal acknowledgement that a small percentage of requests may transit through our US region for cache-warmup during peak hours. That would require legal signoff on a limited routing exception tied to the TIA.

Kimberly / Marissa — can you review the attached template and flag anything we shouldn’t provide or that needs redaction? If we can get a 48-hour turnaround on the template back from Montclair, we can push the package to Legal for a formal TIA addendum.

Alex
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: uk-idta-evidence-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), sccs-to-ukidta-bridge-mapping.pdf (reference)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Julie Park <julie@montclairbio.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: UK IDTA evidence mapping + proposed SLA exception

Alex / Julie —

Thanks, Alex. Quick read-through notes:
- The template looks good as a customer-facing intake. I'll add a column for "sensitivity note" so we can call out items that require redaction (PII examples, raw logs that include token payloads).
- On subprocessors: please confirm whether Montclair expects a full subprocessor chain or just those that touch UK data. For the UK IDTA we generally provide list + roles; if they need subprocessors' SOC2/ISO attestations we'll need formal consent.
- Routing/SLA exception: functionally, we do allow cache-warmup routes to US for <1.5% of requests under cold-start on certain model configs. We can provide a bounded exception in the TIA IF: (a) Montclair accepts the transit risk in writing, and (b) we add encryption-at-rest and request-level logging evidence.

Marissa — tagging you because procurement asked for the routing exception language (short, bulletized) not long-form redlines. Can you draft a one-paragraph approval + limitation we can show to the customer? Also confirm whether an internal SLA exception requires Exec sign-off for this account.

K

Alex / Kimberly / Marissa —

Thanks — that's exactly what procurement wanted. Quick answers:
- Pilot will be limited to production for UK customers only (no staging traffic in scope).
- We'll fill the template and return by EOD Thursday (UK time).
- On the routing exception: Montclair would accept a narrowly scoped transit acknowledgement if you can provide (i) clear upper bound on expected % of transit traffic, (ii) encryption assertions, and (iii) assurance that no UK personal data is stored outside the UK beyond cache TTL (we expect TTL <= 15 minutes).

I'll have procurement attach their procurement contact info to the completed template so you can route redlines directly. Appreciate the quick turnaround here — our timeline is tight for this pilot.

Julie
Director, IT & Security
Montclair Bio

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Julie Park <julie@montclairbio.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: UK IDTA evidence mapping + proposed SLA exception

Hi team —

Draft approval language below that procurement can show Montclair. It's intentionally short so it fits in procurement summaries; Legal can provide full redlines afterward.

"Redwood confirms that, for the Montclair Bio pilot scoped to UK production traffic, a limited routing exception may occur for a small percentage of requests (not to exceed 1.5% of total monthly requests), strictly for cache-warmup behavior. Redwood will: (1) encrypt data in transit and at rest using AES-256; (2) ensure transient request-level logs are retained for 30 days and are accessible for audit; (3) not persist UK personal data outside of EU/UK regions beyond a cache TTL of 15 minutes. This exception is time-bound to the pilot period and requires a signed TIA addendum."
Notes:
- Exec signoff: not required for this single-account pilot under $100k ARR, but Product must sign off on any increased traffic thresholds.
- Subprocessors: we will provide the standard subprocessor list; any third-party attestations (SOC2 reports) will be provided under an NDA if requested.

If that works, Alex can share this paragraph with Montclair and attach the evidence template. Kimberly / Alex — I'll follow up with a short redline bundle for the TIA addendum if procurement pushes for formal language.

Marissa
VP, Privacy & Legal
Redwood Inference
